questions.question: An atom has 17 protons and 18 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 17 + 18 = 35
workingSteps: Step 1: Mass number = Number of protons + Number of neutrons
Step 2: Protons = 17, Neutrons = 18
Step 3: Mass number = 17 + 18 = 35

questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of sodium (Na, atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons arranged as 2 in first shell, 8 in second shell, 1 in third shell
workingSteps: Step 1: Sodium has atomic number 11, so 11 electrons
Step 2: First shell can hold maximum 2 electrons
Step 3: Second shell can hold maximum 8 electrons
Step 4: Remaining 1 electron goes to third shell: 2, 8, 1

questions.question: What type of bond exists in sodium chloride (NaCl)?
questions.explanation: NaCl is formed by electron transfer from Na to Cl, creating ionic bond
workingSteps: Step 1: Na loses 1 electron to become Na⁺
Step 2: Cl gains 1 electron to become Cl⁻
Step 3: Electrostatic attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻
Step 4: This is an ionic bond

questions.question: Two isotopes of chlorine are ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl. They differ in their number of:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
workingSteps: Step 1: Both isotopes have atomic number 17 (same protons)
Step 2: ³⁵Cl has mass number 35, ³⁷Cl has mass number 37
Step 3: Neutrons in ³⁵Cl = 35 - 17 = 18
Step 4: Neutrons in ³⁷Cl = 37 - 17 = 20 (different)

questions.question: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same:
questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons
workingSteps: Step 1: Groups are vertical columns in periodic table
Step 2: Elements in same group have similar properties
Step 3: This is because they have same number of valence electrons
Step 4: Valence electrons determine chemical behavior

questions.question: Balance the equation: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O balances with 4H and 2O on each side
workingSteps: Step 1: Count atoms on each side
Step 2: Left: 2H, 2O; Right: 2H, 1O (unbalanced)
Step 3: Put coefficient 2 before H₂O: H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
Step 4: Put coefficient 2 before H₂: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (balanced)

questions.question: The reaction CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ is an example of:
questions.explanation: One compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances
workingSteps: Step 1: Identify reactants and products
Step 2: One reactant (CaCO₃) breaks into two products
Step 3: This is characteristic of decomposition reaction
Step 4: General form: AB → A + B

questions.question: In the reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, which element is oxidized?
questions.explanation: Zn loses electrons (0 to +2 oxidation state), so it is oxidized
workingSteps: Step 1: Determine oxidation states
Step 2: Zn: 0 → +2 (loses electrons)
Step 3: Cu: +2 → 0 (gains electrons)
Step 4: Loss of electrons = oxidation, so Zn is oxidized

questions.question: What is the pH of a solution with [H⁺] = 1 × 10⁻³ M?
workingSteps: Step 1: pH = -log[H⁺]
Step 3: pH = -log(1 × 10⁻³)

questions.question: How many moles of O₂ are needed to react with 2 moles of H₂ in: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O?
questions.explanation: From the balanced equation, 2 moles H₂ react with 1 mole O₂
workingSteps: Step 1: Write balanced equation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
Step 2: Mole ratio H₂ : O₂ = 2 : 1
Step 3: If 2 moles H₂ react, then O₂ needed = 2 × (1/2)
Step 4: O₂ needed = 1 mole

sections.name: States of Matter and Gas Laws

questions.question: According to kinetic theory, gas molecules:
questions.explanation: Gas molecules move randomly in all directions with high kinetic energy
workingSteps: Step 1: Kinetic theory describes gas behavior
Step 2: Gas molecules are far apart (not closely packed)
Step 3: Intermolecular forces are negligible
Step 4: Molecules move randomly in all directions

questions.question: If the pressure of a gas is doubled at constant temperature, its volume:
questions.explanation: Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. If P doubles, V halves
workingSteps: Step 1: Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (at constant T)
Step 2: If P₂ = 2P₁, then P₁V₁ = 2P₁V₂
Step 3: Divide both sides by P₁: V₁ = 2V₂
Step 4: Therefore V₂ = V₁/2 (volume halves)

questions.question: A gas occupies 100 mL at 27°C. What volume will it occupy at 127°C (pressure constant)?
questions.explanation: Using Charles' Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂
workingSteps: Step 1: Convert temperatures to Kelvin
Step 3: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂, so 100/300 = V₂/400

questions.question: Which of the following represents the ideal gas equation?
questions.explanation: PV = nRT is the ideal gas equation combining all gas laws
workingSteps: Step 1: Ideal gas equation combines Boyle's, Charles', and Avogadro's laws
Step 2: P = pressure, V = volume, n = moles, R = gas constant, T = temperature
Step 3: PV = nRT is the complete form
Step 4: Other options are specific gas laws for constant conditions

questions.question: At STP, one mole of any gas occupies:
questions.explanation: At STP (0°C, 1 atm), one mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L
workingSteps: Step 1: STP = Standard Temperature and Pressure
Step 2: STP conditions: 0°C (273 K) and 1 atm pressure
Step 3: Avogadro's law: equal moles of gases occupy equal volumes
Step 4: Molar volume at STP = 22.4 L/mol

questions.question: The general formula for alkanes is:
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
workingSteps: Step 1: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons (single bonds only)
Step 2: Examples: CH₄ (n=1), C₂H₆ (n=2), C₃H₈ (n=3)
Step 3: Pattern: for n carbons, hydrogens = 2n + 2
Step 4: General formula: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂

questions.question: The functional group in alcohols is:
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group (-OH)
workingSteps: Step 1: Identify functional groups
Step 2: -COOH is carboxyl group (carboxylic acids)
Step 3: -CHO is aldehyde group
Step 4: -OH is hydroxyl group (alcohols)

questions.question: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements are called:
questions.explanation: Isomers have same molecular formula but different structural arrangements
workingSteps: Step 1: Same molecular formula = same number and type of atoms
Step 2: Different structural arrangements = different connectivity
Step 3: This defines isomerism
Step 4: Examples: butane and methylpropane (both C₄H₁₀)

questions.question: Complete combustion of methane produces:
questions.explanation: Complete combustion produces CO₂ and H₂O
workingSteps: Step 1: Complete combustion equation: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
Step 2: Carbon is completely oxidized to CO₂
Step 3: Hydrogen is oxidized to H₂O
Step 4: Products are CO₂ and H₂O

questions.question: The process of joining small molecules to form large molecules is called:
questions.explanation: Polymerization is the process of joining monomers to form polymers
workingSteps: Step 1: Small molecules = monomers
Step 2: Large molecules = polymers
Step 3: Process of joining = polymerization
Step 4: Example: ethene → polyethene

practiceAnswers.11: C - move randomly in all directions
